hints.text: The small raised $3$ is not a multiplier. It tells you how many copies of $5$ to multiply together.
$5^3$ means $5 \times 5 \times 5$. Start with $5 \times 5 = 25$, then multiply that result by the last $5$.

explanation: The exponent counts the copies of the base, so $5^3 = 5 \times 5 \times 5$.
Multiply step by step: $5 \times 5 = 25$, and then $25 \times 5 = 125$.
So $5^3 = 125$. It is not $5 \times 3 = 15$, which is a common mistake.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture a cube
steps: Picture $5^3$ as the number of small blocks in a cube that is $5$ by $5$ by $5$.
One flat layer of the cube holds $5 \times 5 = 25$ blocks.
The cube has $5$ of these layers, so it holds $25 \times 5 = 125$ blocks.

alternativeExplanations.title: Break 25 apart
steps: After $5 \times 5 = 25$, the last multiplication is $25 \times 5$, which is easier if you split $25$ into $20 + 5$.
Multiply each part by $5$ on its own, which gives $20 \times 5 = 100$ and $5 \times 5 = 25$.
Add the parts to get $100 + 25 = 125$, so $5^3 = 125$.
